papers_completed_in_this_checkpoint.title: Relationship lending and the use of trade credit: the role of relational capital and private information

claim_method_alignment.direct_findings: Close and long-lived bank relationships are positively associated with supplier trade credit; the association is stronger where private information and relational-capital proxies are present.
claim_method_alignment.method: Italian manufacturing-firm survey and balance-sheet data for 1995–2006; OLS, alternative measures, propensity-score matching, and 2SLS using historical banking-regulation instruments; mechanism-oriented subsample tests.
claim_method_alignment.identification_boundary: The authors state that the methods only partially address endogeneity; historical-instrument exclusion, old Italian manufacturing data, firm self-reports, and absent supplier-side data constrain causal and external claims.
claim_method_alignment.rhetorical_architecture: Competing substitution/complementarity theories → relationship-lending hypothesis → baseline associations → matching and historical-IV checks → private-information/relational-capital decomposition → bounded policy and data limits.

proposed_atomic_observations: Funding channels can be complements when information and relational capital acquired in one relationship improve access in another; substitution should not be assumed from channel labels alone.
Relationship length, main-bank financing share, number of banking relationships, soft-information exchange, and relational capital are related but non-equivalent constructs.
Matching and historical instruments can strengthen an observational association while leaving exclusion restrictions, reverse causality, and geographic-era generalization as live boundaries.
Mechanism evidence based on opacity and relational-capital subsamples should be expressed as channel-consistent heterogeneity, not as complete causal mediation.

papers_completed_in_this_checkpoint.title: Computing corporate bond returns: a word (or two) of caution

claim_method_alignment.direct_findings: Total corporate-bond returns combine risk-free-rate and credit components that are negatively correlated; TRACE and index datasets materially differ in coverage, alignment, and pricing quality, with TRACE returns showing more negative serial correlation and lagging index information.
claim_method_alignment.method: Return decomposition; exhaustive coding of 65 papers; ICE/BAML–WRDS/TRACE overlap analysis for 2002–2020; duration-matched Treasury adjustment; coverage reconciliation; serial-correlation and lead-lag tests.
claim_method_alignment.identification_boundary: No source is perfect; index data are costly and use provider pricing; TRACE filtering improves relevance but changes the target population and can reduce sample size.
claim_method_alignment.rhetorical_architecture: Define the estimand → expose common return-measure error → quantify literature prevalence → reconcile vendor coverage → test alignment, staleness, and lead-lag quality → prescribe measurement and triangulation rules.

proposed_atomic_observations: When an observed return combines rate and credit components that covary negatively, using the aggregate measure can add noise or reverse inference about the target credit component.
Subtracting a short Treasury-bill return or adding a market-rate control does not replace bond-specific maturity- or duration-matched removal of interest-rate exposure.
Data-provider coverage defines a sample and economic target: more securities is not automatically broader relevant coverage when inclusion rules, liquidity, and instrument types differ.

Calendar alignment, trade staleness, bid-ask bounce, serial correlation, and cross-provider lead-lag behavior are distinct data-quality dimensions; triangulation is stronger than treating one feed as truth.

papers_completed_in_this_checkpoint.title: Stock liquidity, financial constraints, and innovation in Chinese SMEs

claim_method_alignment.direct_findings: For 785 Shenzhen GEM SMEs during 2010–2020, lower quoted spreads are associated with greater R&D spending and patent output; financing access is the principal supported channel, M&A mediation is weak, and patent-output evidence is concentrated in manufacturing.
claim_method_alignment.method: Pooled panel OLS with industry/year controls and clustered errors; alternative liquidity and innovation measures; Fama–MacBeth, quantile, Tobit, Poisson, negative-binomial, fixed-effects, system-GMM, lag/change, and 2SLS checks; financing and M&A channel tests.
claim_method_alignment.identification_boundary: The study lacks a clean exogenous policy shock and acknowledges unresolved endogeneity; the liquidity instruments are assumption-dependent; the sample is one Chinese growth market and is dominated by manufacturing and IT firms.
claim_method_alignment.rhetorical_architecture: Opposed prior findings → multiple candidate mechanisms → input/output construct separation → baseline association → extensive model/proxy robustness → horizon and industry heterogeneity → financing and M&A channel tests → explicit causal and geographic limits.

proposed_atomic_observations: Innovation input and innovation output are different outcomes: R&D expenditure and patent production can differ in magnitude, lag, industry reach, and mechanism support.
A liquidity–innovation association can be consistent with reduced financing constraints while blockholder incentives and M&A channels remain separate, weak, or oppositely signed.
Robustness across estimators and proxies does not create exogenous identification; causal wording remains bounded when reverse causality and instrument validity are unresolved.
A relationship that persists across lags but varies by industry should retain both its horizon and industry scope rather than being summarized as a universal long-run firm effect.
